chunks: And Ẓarīf ibn Nāṣiḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
Abū ʿAbdِ اللهِ عليه السلام said: “If a man were to strike another man with a piece of pottery or with a brick, and he died, it would be considered intentional.”

key_terms.بِآجُرَّةٍ: with a brick; another example of an object whose use may lead to liability for intentional killing
key_terms.بِخَزَفَةٍ: with a piece of pottery; an example of a striking object used in the assault
key_terms.مُتَعَمِّدًا: intentional; legally classified as deliberate rather than accidental

ai.seo_question: When is killing by striking with an object like pottery or a brick considered intentional in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling in the law of homicide: if a person strikes another with an object such as pottery or a brick and death results, the act is treated as intentional killing. Its significance lies in defining legal liability in qisas and related penal rulings based on the nature of the assault and its fatal outcome.
